findings.evidence: "important not because a single kilowatt-hour is meaningful by itself, but because every downstream cost and capacity number is denominated in it — or, for non-autoregressive generation, in model evaluations"
findings.issue: Ambiguous pronoun 'it' in 'denominated in it': the nearest antecedent is 'a single kilowatt-hour' (inside the dash-enclosed clause), but the intended referent is 'a token' (the sentence's overall subject/metaphor). A reader parsing linearly may momentarily resolve 'it' to kilowatt-hour before correcting.
findings.fix_instruction: Replace 'denominated in it' with an explicit noun: 'denominated in tokens' (or 'denominated in a token').

findings.evidence: "MLA ≈57× less for DeepSeek-class geometry, inside a ~50–60× band"
findings.issue: Phrasing '57× less' is technically imprecise under ASD-STE100: 'X× less' is ambiguous (subtract X times? or divide by X?). The correct technical phrasing is '57× smaller' or '1/57th the size.' This pattern recurs at least twice more: '~5.5× less compute' (PDF p.61, Ch.3 §3.3.3) and '~12× less per-token weight traffic' (PDF p.67, Ch.3 §3.6.1).
findings.fix_instruction: Replace all 'X× less' with 'X× smaller' or rephrase as 'reduced by a factor of X' / '1/X the size.' Scan full document for remaining instances.

findings.chapter: Ch. 1 — It All Starts With the First Token
findings.evidence: Page 23: "[1P][FACT] model cards: HF Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next; HF zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash; DeepSeek-V4 technical report, arXiv 2606.19348, and model card HF deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro — all accessed 2026-08-30, the book's evidence cutoff; A.10". Page 94 (Ch. 4 Table 4-2): "H100 HBM per GPU | 80 GB | [1P][FACT] NVIDIA H100 SXM5 datasheet (80 GB HBM3)". Page 121 (Ch. 6 Table 6-1) footnote: "the hardware constants — H100 dense BF16 peak ~0.989 PFLOPS without sparsity, HBM3 peak ~3.35 TB/s — take their first-party provenance from the NVIDIA H100 datasheet (SXM5), named here as in Table 8-1".
findings.issue: Two distinct first-party sources are cited for the same [1P][FACT] hardware constants in two different formats — an inline 'NVIDIA H100 SXM5 datasheet' in Ch. 4 and a bracketed key '(SXM5)' pointing at Table 8-1 in Ch. 6 — while the vendor model cards in Ch. 1 use a third, unrelated citation style ('A.10'). The book defines a bracketed source-key system on p. 137: "each [S#] names one entry in the References chapter, and the keys are book-wide, [S1]–[S7]", yet the NVIDIA datasheet is never given an [S#] key; a reader following the [S1]–[S7] scheme cannot resolve the hardware constant. Meanwhile Ch. 1's 'A.10' pointer refers to an Appendix A section whose existence and numbering is not verifiable from the front matter (the Contents lists only 'Appendix A — ...' as one entry, and no A.10 sub-section listing exists in the front matter at all).
findings.fix_instruction: Add the NVIDIA H100 SXM5 datasheet to the References chapter under a book-wide [S#] key (e.g. [S8]) and cite it by that key everywhere it is used; and add a per-section list of Appendix A subsections (A.1–A.n) to the front matter so 'A.10' pointers resolve.

findings.evidence: Page 27: "The vLLM FP8-KV blog post's often-quoted '54%' — from its Llama-3.1-8B Table 3 (vLLM blog, post dated 2026-04-22 — inside the 2026-08-30 evidence cutoff; retrieved 2026-11-15, an access date only, since access dates are not evidence dates, so no addendum revision applies) [S6] — is, on this book's reading of that table, a decode inter-token-latency (ITL) slope, not a memory ratio or footprint coefficient [1P][DERIVED]. That reading is the book's own, not a vendor-stated interpretation; re-verify it against the post."
findings.issue: The label pair is mismatched to the sentence. The claim being made is a first-party reading of a first-party table ('is ... a decode ITL slope'), but the tag attached is [1P][DERIVED] — i.e. it asserts a derivation rather than a source-stated fact — while the text immediately says 'That reading is the book's own, not a vendor-stated interpretation'. A vendor-stated fact would be [1P][FACT]; a book's own reading of a vendor table that the book does not reproduce is an interpretation, not a derivation from stated inputs. [DERIVED] is defined (p. 17) as 'computed by arithmetic from stated inputs', which this is not.
findings.fix_instruction: Relabel this claim as [1P][HYPOTHESIS] (the book's own reading, not yet validated by the vendor), or [2°][HYPOTHESIS], and reserve [1P][DERIVED] for arithmetic actually performed on stated inputs. If the book intends to keep [1P], add the arithmetic that produces the ITL-slope reading so the tag matches the definition.

findings.evidence: Page 27: "At 9.2K tokens the canonical FP16 KV per request is ~24.1 GB — 9,200 × 2,621,440 B = 24,117,248,000 B ≈ 24.12 GB — and the 8-bit raw byte-halving variant is ~12.06 GB — 9,200 × 1,310,720 B = 12,058,624,000 B ≈ 12.06 GB ... [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]"
findings.issue: The label [ILLUSTRATIVE] is wrong for this figure. This row is the canonical scenario's own KV residency — the Preface (p. 17) states explicitly: 'the canonical scenario (Ch. 4, Table 4-2) keeps its own [canonical scenario] provenance' and that within it a derived value is [canonical scenario][DERIVED]. The book's own canonical KV constant is 2.62 MB/token and 24.1 GB at 9.2K (repeated on pp. 31, 42, 62, 65, 84, 100, 106, 118, 146–148). Tagging this particular statement [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] makes the canonical number non-canonical at one of its primary occurrences, contradicting Table 4-2 (p. 93: 'KV per token (FP16, MHA) | 2,621,440 B ≈ 2.62 MB | [canonical scenario][DERIVED]').
findings.fix_instruction: Change the tag on the 24.1 GB / 12.06 GB KV residency derivation to [canonical scenario][DERIVED], matching Table 4-2 and every other occurrence of the same number.

findings.evidence: Page 29, Fig 1.1 caption: "figure 1.1: The KV cache: every token adds one K/V per layer per head — for a generated token, written when that token is next processed as input, one step after it is sampled; prompt-token K/V is written during prefill. This is a single-layer detail view: one layer's stored K and stored V drawn separately, each enumerated per head (h₁–h₄) ... [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] conceptual".
findings.issue: The caption is labeled [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION], but the figure depicts a mechanism (when K/V enters the cache) that the book's own body text states as fact (p. 36: "A token's K/V therefore enters the cache on the step in which it is the input, not on the step in which it is sampled"; p. 16 in the same chapter: the KV cache is 'the stored key and value tensors for every token in the context'). A conceptual drawing of a mechanism is not an assumption; the [ASSUMPTION] tag on Axis 2 misstates the epistemic status of a documented behavior. The same figure's body text (p. 29) says 'the verified arithmetic is Ch. 7's' — i.e. the chapter itself asserts the arithmetic is verified elsewhere, which contradicts tagging the figure's own content as assumed.
findings.fix_instruction: Retag Fig 1.1 as [ILLUSTRATIVE][FACT] (conceptual rendering of a documented mechanism) or split the tag: [ILLUSTRATIVE] for the drawing's form and [1P][FACT] for the cache-write timing, and state in the caption that the numbers are verified in Ch. 7.

findings.evidence: Page 26 table: "Reduced-width per-token | yes, linearly | MLA-style latent attention, GQA, MQA head sharing | fewer than full MHA (MLA ≈57× less for DeepSeek-class geometry, inside a ~50–60× band: 2·n_h·d_h = 2×128×128 = 32,768 dims per layer per token for full MHA vs d_c + d_h^R = 512+64 = 576 for MLA, 32,768/576 ≈ 56.9 ≈ 57×; geometry n_h = 128, d_h = 128, d_c = 512, d_h^R = 64 as specified in DeepSeek's MLA report (DeepSeek-V2, arXiv:2405.04434) [1P][DERIVED])"
findings.issue: Two problems. (a) The tag [1P][DERIVED] is applied to a paragraph that mixes a first-party geometry (the DeepSeek-V2 numbers) with an arithmetic result (32,768/576 ≈ 57×) and an editorial characterization ('inside a ~50–60× band') that is neither a source statement nor a derivation — it is the book's own characterization, which by the book's own Axis-2 definitions is [HYPOTHESIS] or [DERIVED], not [1P]. (b) The '~50–60× band' is stated with no source; it is presented inside a cell tagged [1P][DERIVED], i.e. as if the band were in the DeepSeek-V2 report. The report is cited for geometry only.
findings.fix_instruction: Split the cell: attribute the geometry to [1P][FACT] (DeepSeek-V2, arXiv:2405.04434), the 32,768/576 ≈ 57× ratio to [1P][DERIVED], and either source the '~50–60× band' explicitly or retag it [HYPOTHESIS] so it is not carried under a first-party label.

findings.evidence: Page 31: "If average request is ~9.2K input + ~300 output ≈ 9.5K tokens per request ... Roughly 30× more input tokens than output tokens in this workload (9,200 ÷ 300 ≈ 30.7, carried book-wide as the canonical ~30×, Ch. 4, Table 4-2)." Table 1-1 rows: 'input tokens/s @ 10 rps | ~92,000 | 9,200 ×10'; 'input tokens/s @ peak 40 rps | ~368,000 | 9,200 ×40'. Page 84 (Canonical Workload box): 'Average arrival rate | ~10 rps'; 'Peak arrival rate | ~40 rps'.
findings.issue: The arithmetic checks (9,200×10 = 92,000; 9,200×40 = 368,000; 9,200÷300 ≈ 30.7). The defect is terminological: the book repeatedly writes '9.2K' with the K as a thousands shorthand for token counts (pp. 31, 42, 84, 106, 115, 118, 148) while the Preface (p. 20) states 'the SI convention applies: K = 1,000 and M = 1,000,000 for token counts' — so '9.2K' is correct — but the same shorthand is then reused for context-length variants where the arithmetic uses a different basis: page 90 writes '32K means 32,000' while page 106 and 108 mix '9.2K input' with '~32K context' and '~9.5K input+output'. Since 9.2K/9.5K are *nominal* (9,200 / 9,500) but the chapter also prints them as '~9.2K' with a tilde, the tilde is doing double duty as 'approximately' and as part of the notation. In the canonical box (p. 84) the book handles this properly by stating 'the token-count rows (1,200 / 8,000 / 9,200 / 300) are the same kind of approximate canonical input and carry the same status even though the tilde is not repeated' — the reader must carry that caveat into every later chapter, where the tilde IS sometimes repeated and sometimes not for the same numbers.
findings.fix_instruction: Adopt one notation for the canonical token counts — e.g. write '9,200 tokens (9.2K)' at first use in each chapter and use '9.2K' thereafter — and stop mixing the tilde-prefixed and tilde-free forms of the same canonical values across chapters, or state the convention once per chapter rather than relying on a note in Ch. 4's box.

findings.evidence: Page 21 is the Part I divider page: 'part I. / The Token / 1'. Page 22 is the Chapter 1 opening page: 'chapter 1. / It All Starts With the First Token ... 2' with 'The Architect's Question' section, and page 23 continues '3'. The Contents (p. 6) lists 'I The Token 1' and '1 It All Starts With the First Token 2'.
findings.issue: The Contents gives Part I a start page of 1 and Chapter 1 a start page of 2, but the printed pages carry different numbers: the Part I divider is PDF page 21 while the chapter-1 title page is PDF page 22 and its first numbered text page is PDF page 23 (showing '3'). Because the front matter (title, copyright, contents, figures, preface) runs to PDF page 20 and is numbered with roman numerals (iv, vii, xi...), the PDF page 21 should be printed page 1 — but the page images provided for the sampled pages show the running head 'Understanding the Model ... 38' on PDF page 57 and 'Memory Is the First Constraint ... 134' on PDF page 153, i.e. printed page = PDF page − 19. So PDF page 21 = printed page 2, and the Part I divider would be printed page 2, contradicting the Contents' 'I The Token 1'.
findings.fix_instruction: Recompute the printed-page offsets for the front matter and verify the Contents page numbers for Part I, Part II (55), Part III (122), Part IV (226), Part V (311) and Part VI (397) against the actual printed folios; fix whichever set is wrong.

findings.evidence: Page 29, Fig 1.1 caption: "for a generated token, written when that token is next processed as input, one step after it is sampled; prompt-token K/V is written during prefill." Page 36 (Ch. 2 §2.1): "(d) the sampled next token is the output of this step and the input of the following step, whose forward pass then computes and appends its K/V. A token's K/V therefore enters the cache on the step in which it is the input, not on the step in which it is sampled."
findings.issue: The two statements are consistent, but Fig 1.1's label set ('end of prefill', 'first decode', 'second decode', 'later decode') and its arrows ('append K/V', 'store K', 'store V', 'read K', 'read V', 'read for attention') do not distinguish the 'sampled token' from the 'input token' — so the figure's geometry does not itself show the one-step offset the caption describes, while the caption is careful to specify it. The defect is one of caption-vs-figure correspondence: a caption asserting a timing detail ('one step after it is sampled') that the drawing's token labels cannot express.
findings.fix_instruction: Add a 'sampled' vs 'input' distinction to Fig 1.1's token sequence (e.g. label token₂ as 'token₁ sampled → token₂ input') so the one-step offset the caption describes is visible in the drawing, or restate the caption as a text note rather than as a description of the figure's geometry.

findings.evidence: Page 29 Fig 1.1 is a 'single-layer detail view'; page 40 Fig 2.1 shows the full pipeline with 'PREFILL', 'DECODE' and 'PERSISTENT KV CACHE' boxes and the caption states: 'The two bands and the single PERSISTENT KV CACHE box are conceptual groupings for teaching, not runtime components: a real serving stack has per-layer, per-request KV state and no literal "prefill band" object.'
findings.issue: Fig 2.1's caption is exemplary on the point. The defect is that Fig 1.1's caption does not carry the analogous note that its 'layer L · h₁–h₄' enumeration is a schematic of one layer, so a reader may read the figure as showing the model's actual head count (the canonical model has 64 query heads and 64 KV heads; the figure shows 4 heads: h₁–h₄). The caption does say 'This is a single-layer detail view' and 'The head glyphs are schematic' appears in Fig 7.1's caption (p. 152) — but not in Fig 1.1's. Since the canonical model's head count is 64 (Table 4-2, p. 92), a figure showing four heads without a schematic note can be misread as the model's geometry.
findings.fix_instruction: Add 'head glyphs are schematic (the canonical model has 64 query and 64 KV heads per layer)' to Fig 1.1's caption, matching Fig 7.1's treatment.

findings.evidence: Page 31: "Worked example, not reference. If average request is ~9.2K input + ~300 output ≈ 9.5K tokens per request, and traffic is ~10 req/s, then the system ingests: ... Input tokens/s: 9,200 tokens/req × 10 req/s = 92,000 tokens/s (peaks higher at ~40 req/s → ~368k)." Page 84 (Canonical Workload box): "The active-hours volume is ~6.24M requests/month".
findings.issue: The arithmetic checks (92,000; 368,000; 3,000). The defect is that Ch. 1 §1.3 says 'traffic is ~10 req/s' and derives the hourly rates, then Ch. 4 §4.3's canonical box reveals that 10 rps is 'the rate over the active business-hours window (an 8-hour × 260-workday schedule), not 24×7 wall-clock' — a qualifier Ch. 1 cannot know but does not flag. A reader who reads Ch. 1's 'the system ingests 92,000 tokens/s' as a 24×7 figure will read Ch. 4's '$87,600/mo (730 h/mo) vs $20,800/mo (173.3 active h/mo)' as a contradiction rather than a duty-cycle distinction. Ch. 1 introduces no duty-cycle caveat at all.
findings.fix_instruction: Add a one-line forward pointer in Ch. 1 §1.3 noting that the canonical traffic rate is an active-hours average (Ch. 4), so the token rates are not 24×7 fleet rates.

findings.evidence: Page 25: "the L² term is a prefill cost — it describes computing attention across all position pairs in one pass over the full input. During decode, each generated token attends once to the growing prefix, so the per-token step is a linear cost in context length — an attention term that is per-step compute".
findings.issue: The statement is correct in shape, but the arithmetic-intensity consequence (which the book itself derives later) is not carried here, and this is where the '~1 FLOP/byte' decode attention figure first becomes consequential. With the decode attention intensity at 2 FLOP/byte (full-MHA) rather than the ~1 FLOP/byte the book later uses, the sentence 'the per-step step is a linear cost in context length' is right but its intensity consequence (a linear-in-L FLOP term against a linear-in-L byte term, i.e. a constant intensity of 2 FLOP/byte) is what Ch. 2 and Ch. 6 need. The book instead uses the weight-only ~1 FLOP/byte figure for the whole decode step in Fig 2.2, which conflates the weight-stream term with the attention term.
findings.fix_instruction: In Ch. 1 §1.1.4, add the intensity consequence of the linear-in-L attention term (constant 2 FLOP/byte for full-MHA dense attention, since FLOPs and bytes both scale linearly in L), and make Fig 2.2's decode marker explicitly the weight-stream intensity only (see P1-078).

findings.evidence: Page 30, Fig 1.2 caption: 'figure 1.2: How a token travels: text → tokenizer → IDs → embedding → attention → KV cache. Conceptual only: what is drawn is the one-time token-to-state construction — a one-pass abstraction of how a token becomes state, not the full transformer and not the step-to-step loop. The K/V are produced within every applicable layer (not after a single "attention" stage), and the KV cache is a persistent state — written (append) and read (read past K,V, the backward read arrow from the KV cache back to attention) across steps — not a processing stage. ... [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] conceptual"
findings.issue: The caption's own hedge list is long and contains a self-contradiction in the tag pairing: the body is tagged '[ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] conceptual' — an Axis-2 value (ASSUMPTION) plus an undeclared word ('conceptual'). Per the Preface's declared rule (p. 16) ILLUSTRATIVE must be 'paired with ASSUMPTION or DERIVED', so the tag form complies; but the appended 'conceptual' then signals that the assumption is of a different kind (a conceptual diagram, not a scenario input), which the Axis-2 vocabulary has no value for. The same pattern recurs at p. 47 ('[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual, roofline developed in Ch 8]'), p. 111 ('[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual]'), p. 134 ('[ILLUSTRATIVE synthetic profile]') and p. 187 area — so 'conceptual' and 'synthetic profile' are being used as unregistered Axis-2 qualifiers across at least four figures.
findings.fix_instruction: Register 'conceptual' and 'synthetic profile' as named Axis-2 qualifiers in the Preface (or add them to the Sources chapter's label table), and apply them uniformly; alternatively drop them and use only the five declared Axis-2 values so that every figure's tag pair is drawn from one closed list.
